newsitem.title: USA: Alliant ends work on US Air Force project.
newsitem.headline: Alliant ends work on US Air Force project.

text.p: Alliant Techsystems Inc on Friday said it was not among the two teams selected by the U.S. Air Force to work on the second stage of development of the Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle (EELV).

An Alliant spokesman said two $60 million contracts were at stake. The Air Force selected Lockheed Martin Corp and McDonnell Douglas Corp for the 17-month EELV pre-engineering and manufacturing development part of the project, Alliant said.
Alliant was among several contractors that completed work on the first phase of the EELV project in September.

Alliant Techsystems said the company was on track to achieve its goal of boosting earnings per share at an average annual rate of 15 percent in spite of not being selected to participate in the second phase Two of the EELV project.
"The EELV program was certainly a very significant opportunity and one that we wanted to win," Alliant President and Chief Executive Officer Richard Schwartz said.

Schwartz added that Alliant still had long-term contracts and options to supply motors for the Delta, Titan and Pegasus space launch vehicles and for the Trident ballistic missile. Those programs are expected to run for the next 10 years.
